{{short description|American statistician}}
{{use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2020}}
'''Lori A. Thombs''' is an American statistician whose interests include [[social statistics]], [[time series]], and [[Resampling (statistics)|resampling]]. She is an associate professor of statistics at the [[University of Missouri]], where she directs the Social Science Statistics Center,{{r|mizzou}} and president of the Southern Regional Council On Statistics.{{r|srcos}}

==Education and career==
Thombs is a 1981 graduate of [[Baylor University]],{{r|cv}} and completed a Ph.D. in statistics at [[Southern Methodist University]] in 1985.{{r|mizzou}} Her dissertation, ''Bootstrap Prediction Intervals for Autoregression'', was supervised by William R. Schucany.{{r|cv|mg}}

She joined the statistics department at the [[University of South Carolina]], in [[Columbia, South Carolina]], in 1985, and moved to the University of Missouri, in [[Columbia, Missouri]], in 2003.{{r|cv|twocol}}

She was elected president of the Southern Regional Council On Statistics in 2018.{{r|srcos}}

==Books==
Thombs is a coauthor, with Don Edwards and John D. Spurrier, of the books ''Elementary Statistics Laboratory Manual'' (in two versions, Wadsworth, 1995) and ''Statistics: Learning by Doing'' (Whittier, 1999). She is a coeditor, with  Stanislav Kolenikov and Douglas Steinle, of ''Statistics in the Social Sciences: Current Methodological Developments'' (Wiley, 2010).{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Thombs was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2011.{{r|cv|fasa}}
